steps.text: Whisk teriyaki sauce, lemon juice, garlic, and sesame oil together in a bowl

Pour marinade into a resealable plastic bag. Add chicken, coat with marinade, squeeze out excess air, and seal the bag. Marinate in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour to overnight, turning every so often.
When ready to cook, preheat an outdoor grill for high heat and lightly oil the grate. Remove chicken from marinade and shake off excess. Discard any remaining marinade.

Cook chicken breasts on the preheated grill until no longer pink in the center and the juices run clear, 6 to 8 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Grilled Teriyaki Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This grilled teriyaki chicken made with a super easy marinade and cooked to perfection on a hot grill is an easy summer meal that everyone will enjoy.

video.description: Watch this video to see how easy it is to make this favorite 'go-to' take out meal at home. We marinate the chicken overnight in teriyaki sauce before cooking it up on a hot grill.

review.reviewBody: My husband and I loved the recipe. We marinated it for 1 hour and also put 1/2 as much teriyaki sauce and it was delicious. We left 2 pieces of chicken the full 24 hours and it wasn't as tasty as the day before. I hope this helps! All in all it was really tasty.

I was hungry for chicken teriyaki so I only marinated it for about 5 hours. I didn't have sesame seed oil, so I left that out. Anyway, the chicken tasted great; the flavor went all through it. It was very moist and tender, too. I used about 3/4 cup of teriyaki sauce and everything else in the same proportions, although I had plenty of marinade for 6 chicken breast halves instead of four.

I used about 3/4 cup of teriyaki sauce with sesame seeds already in it, 2 tsp. lime juice, a hearty squeeze of honey from the bottle, 2 tbs. minced garlic, and a small can of pineapple chunks(including the juice). These were the things I had on hand (no sesame oil). I marinaded chicken tenderloin strips in this for about 2 hours. I sprayed the grill with olive oil then put the chicken and pineapple chunks on skewers and grilled them. The whole family enjoyed this yummy "chicken on a stick."

Even marinated for one hour, this recipe was excellent. I added some sweet thai chili sauce for a little spicy kick. I saved the marinade and stir fried it with some cooked spaghetti noodles and made a bed of the noodles for the chicken to lay on. This is definately a family favorite.
Very easy to prepare and so so results. I found the Teriyaki taste to be too strong. I only used 1/2 Cup of the Teriyaki so I can't imagine what the full amount would be!!

This is delicious! I was a bit concerned about it being too salty after I read the previous reviews, so I added a couple of teaspoons of white wine vinegar to the marinade and it was fine (not too salty).

We all really loved this! I had forgotten about the overnight marinade so I only marinaded for 10 hours, still came out great! We had the chicken as sandwiches with lettuce and tomato and I basted the chiccken all throughout the cooking process. Will make again!
Wow, this recipe was really easy and tasted great. I slow cooked the chicken on the grill and it really kept all of it's flavor.

This was yummy and incredibly easy. Using other reviewers' suggestions, I added half a can of pineapple chunks (with the juice) and added a big squirt of honey. I used chicken breast cutlets on the George Foreman grill. I forgot to marinate it overnight but put it in the fridge for about 12 hours. The teriyaki sauce I had on hand had garlic in it so I didn't add more. I also didn't have sesame oil on hand and just went without it. I served it with white rice and if I had had more time, I would've added steamed broccoli.

This was an awesome recipe! I followed the ingredients but made 3/4 of the recipe and had plenty of sauce. I saved about 1/4 cup and basted the chicken as it was cooking on the BBQ. We loved the flavor, I haven't ever used sesame oil and I couldn't believe how much it changed the flavor (for the better!) This was probably the best chicken that I have ever made on the grill, it was so moist too! Thanks for the great recipe!

GREAT marinade! We really liked it and will make it again. I agree to reduce the teriyaki sauce to 2/3 cup. I used 3/4 c. and it was just slightly too salty still. I added 2 diced green onions/scallions to the marinade and a dash of ginger as suggested by others. This was probably one of the best marinades we have ever had. Only had time to marinade the meat about 2 hours but still perfect.
P.S. I had originally rated this recipe a 4 stars, but my husband asked me to reconsider since he loved it so much. After preparing and eating this again with the same excellent results, I had to agree with him!

Great recipe. I added a little bit of fish sauce and ginger to the marinade. The lemon made the dish great! I did baste it with a small amount of bottled teriyaki sauce as it was cooking on the grill. Everyone in my family enjoyed it.
My picky husband loved it. I loved how easy it was!
Easy and tasty!

The longer this marinates, the better it is! If you have the chance, let it sit for two days or three. The flavor gets in there! Quick easy and delicious! Oyster sauce, plum sauce, hoisin sauce, honey, brown sugar are all great additions. Brown on stove and in oven until done. Did mine in cast iron skillet and when the fridge opened, I saw eyes light up ❣️❣️❣️

It always gets me going when a recipe like this for teriyaki chicken starts with a jar of teriyaki sauce. Why not show how to make the sauce from scratch? It's so simple! Soya sauce Brown sugar Fresh Garlic ginger Fresh garlic Play with the amounts, tweak it, but make it yourself, without all the extra stabilizers, emulsifiers, preservatives and artificial colours.
Excellent recipe, very easy, quick and delicious! The family loves it!

I love teriyaki sauce and was happy to have found this great recipe for grilled chicken. The marinade was spot on with the umami from the teriyaki and the fresh acidity from the lemon juice. And garlic makes everything ten times better anyway. My grill was scorching hot and that hard sear on the marinade was magical, top notch flavors all around.
Great flavor with the crusty top! The first chicken breast entrée that was moist,juicy and very flavorful.
For the teriyaki sauce I used Japanese Barbeque Sauce. I let it marinate overnight. Cooked on the flat grill outside to the recommended 165 internal temp. It was moist, tender and delicious.
